interface.evidence: Original problem interface lists 1024-bit in, 8-bit sel, 4-bit out.

semantics.function: For each output bit b in 0..3, out[b] = in[4*unsigned(sel)+b].
semantics.timing: Pure combinational selection; changes to either input affect output after combinational settling, without clock cycles or added latency.
semantics.reset: No reset port or reset behavior specified.
semantics.initialization: No stored state or specified initial value; output follows the current inputs.
semantics.evidence: Original specifies a 4-bit wide 256-to-1 multiplexer and examples sel=0 -> in[3:0], sel=1 -> in[7:4], sel=2 -> in[11:8].

numeric.data: Packed bit groups; no arithmetic interpretation, rounding, saturation, or overflow.
numeric.selector: Unsigned 8-bit selector, all binary values 0..255 legal.
numeric.ordering: Group zero occupies least significant four bits; final group occupies bits 1023:1020.

verification.oracle: Compute each expected output bit independently from original mapping, using integer group and bit indices.
verification.coverage: All 256 selectors with all 16 nibble values, zero/one backgrounds, walking input bits, random vectors, input changes with fixed sel, selected X/Z data.
verification.sampling: Drive inputs then wait #1 for combinational settling before comparing with case inequality.
verification.failure: $fatal on any mismatch and bounded timeout; PASS only after all checks.
verification.evaluation: python3 dev_check.py --label initial; development evidence only.

specification_ambiguities.evidence: Original gives binary selector examples but does not define X/Z selector handling.
specification_ambiguities.resolution: No extra behavior required or asserted for unknown selector; use standard SystemVerilog indexing semantics.
